fig-deployment-mask.ariaDescription: A row of deployment steps on the left maps by index into bit positions in a uint256 mask on the right. Each step sets its bit only when code exists at that configured address.
fig-deployment-mask.ariaLabel: Deployment mask maps ordered deployment steps to bits

fig-escalation-game-module-split.ariaDescription: A left-hand inheritance chain runs from shared storage and state into calculations, carry, escrow, settlement, and the public game contract. A deposit delegate uses the same storage layout through delegatecall, while a separate proof verifier feeds verified math back into the mutable stack without acquiring storage authority.
fig-escalation-game-module-split.ariaLabel: EscalationGame module split between inherited state modules, the deposit delegate, and the external proof verifier

children.text: delegatecall preserves the game's shared storage surface

fig-invariant-layers.ariaDescription:
Four connected layers run from local authority guards through
							cross-contract conservation and lifecycle liveness to economic
							security. A failure in an earlier layer invalidates the safety
							claims built above it.

children.text: Each layer depends on every invariant to its left.

fig-liquidation-punitive-flow.ariaDescription:
Punitive Flow. The liquidator takes
						debt and receives unlocked REP from the target vault. The target is
						punished, the liquidator is rewarded, and the target becomes
						healthier only because required REP backing falls faster than REP is
						seized. The ordinary path uses bonus-priced REP; a full staged-allowance
						close can instead sweep all current unlocked REP when the ordinary
						conversion would consume all ownership or leave forbidden REP dust.
fig-liquidation-punitive-flow.ariaLabel: Unsafe vault debt and unlocked REP move from the target vault to a non-liquidatable liquidator vault.

fig-liquidation-execution-decision.ariaDescription: A stale price leaves the operation queued. Coordinator expiry, snapshot, or distance failures consume the staged operation without a pool call. After those gates pass, the pool computes capped debt and rounded REP, applies the full-close override when required, and then validates and applies that candidate. A pool-level failure is consumed and emitted as failed; success completes the selected REP transfer.
fig-liquidation-execution-decision.ariaLabel: A staged liquidation selects an ordinary or full-close REP candidate before pool validation either fails or completes the transfer

children.text: cap debt, then round bonus-priced REP
full debt; ownership or forbidden REP dust

fig-mmr-peaks.ariaDescription: A leaf count of thirteen is shown as binary one one zero one, corresponding to occupied peaks at heights zero, two, and three which are later bagged into one root.
fig-mmr-peaks.ariaLabel: Merkle Mountain Range peaks are determined by set bits in the leaf count

fig-mmr-proof-anatomy.ariaDescription: The membership lane combines the carried deposit leaf with bottom-up siblings inside its selected peak, then with other occupied peak roots in ascending height order to reconstruct the snapshot root. The nullifier lane hashes the stable parent deposit index and combines it with a fixed-depth sibling path to prove the claim has not already been consumed.
fig-mmr-proof-anatomy.ariaLabel: A carried-deposit proof has an MMR membership lane and a separate nullifier lane

fig-openoracle-integration-flow.ariaDescription:
Statoblast queues solvency-sensitive operations behind a bounded
							OpenOracle REP/ETH report and executes them only with a fresh
							accepted price.

children.text: fresh price, pending report, and local safety checks
Expired operations, stale liquidations, zero-effect withdrawals,

plot-open-oracle-integration-2.ariaDescription: Binary censorship threshold and cost comparison
plot-open-oracle-integration-2.ariaLabel: Binary censorship threshold and cost comparison

fig-statoblast-actor-swimlanes.ariaDescription:
Trader, vault operator, and protocol responsibilities across
								minting, reporting, forking, migration, auction repair, and
								redemption.

fig-statoblast-asset-flow.ariaDescription:
Users send ETH to the security pool, which mints shares. A
								redemption request goes to the pool; the pool burns the relevant
								shares and pays ETH. Vaults send REP and receive fees; fork
								repair can sell child REP for ETH.
fig-statoblast-asset-flow.ariaLabel: ETH, REP, shares, and fee flow

fig-statoblast-pool-accounting.ariaDescription:
REP deposits mint proportional pool ownership, decayed
								collateral increments the fee index, and vault allowances claim
								fees from that index.

fig-statoblast-share-lifecycle.ariaDescription:
ETH mints Invalid, Yes, and No shares. Operational pools redeem
								full sets, and finalized winning shares redeem through outcome
								settlement.

fig-statoblast-share-migration.ariaDescription:
On first materialization into untouched children, the full current
								parent balance materializes in each selected child token id while
								the source remains locked as an entitlement. Later calls mint only
								the unmaterialized delta for each child.
fig-statoblast-share-migration.ariaLabel: Share migration materializes persistent branch entitlements

fig-statoblast-escalation-cost-curve.ariaDescription: The required bond rises exponentially from the normalized starting bond to one hundred percent of the non-decision threshold over the full escalation interval.
fig-statoblast-escalation-cost-curve.ariaLabel: Exponential escalation bond curve from the starting bond to the non-decision threshold

fig-statoblast-non-decision-flow.ariaDescription:
Outcome balances are compared to running total cost for local
								resolution and to the fixed non-decision threshold for a local
								game's fork eligibility. A pool with an inherited fixed outcome
								rejects both new local deposits and fork activation.

fig-statoblast-payout-regions.ariaDescription:
Winning deposits below binding capital and in the safety
								boundary share rewards, while excess receives principal only.

fig-statoblast-fork-state-machine.ariaDescription:
Contract states and conditional transition functions from an
								operational parent through migration and bounded truth-auction
								settlement to an operational child.

children.text: immediate if no auction is needed

fig-statoblast-migration-flow.ariaDescription:
After a Zoltar fork, Statoblast migrates vaults, collateral, and
								shares. Child creation separately reproduces unresolved escalation
								state and aggregate backing once.

fig-statoblast-migration-proxy.ariaDescription:
The forker controls one deterministic proxy per parent pool, and
								the proxy is the caller recorded by Zoltar migration accounting.

children.text: ledger key = proxy address, not the vault address

fig-statoblast-proportional-migration.ariaDescription:
Parent pool ownership determines migrated REP, and migrated REP
								determines the child collateral transferred from the parent
								collateral baseline.

fig-statoblast-own-fork-rep-buckets.ariaDescription:
Pool REP and unresolved escalation REP enter one Zoltar fork
								balance. Ordinary pool REP remains in the vault bucket at 1:1,
								while the fork haircut is deducted from escalation aggregate backing.

fig-statoblast-recursive-continuation.ariaDescription:
A caller invokes Zoltar to fork a universe while one of its security pools has
								an unresolved escalation. Later, migration into selected child branches deploys child pools
								and initializes paused continuation games. Canonical snapshot state supplies each selected
								child's proof baseline, aggregate REP supplies physical backing once, and
								authenticated winning proofs pay their recorded depositors. Only a
								continuation pool without a fixed outcome may fork again; within that
								boundary, a local non-decision or inherited threshold tie makes its game
								eligible for the security-pool fork path.

fig-statoblast-carry-snapshot.ariaDescription:
Current balances, carry, and nullifiers form the canonical next
								snapshot. Remaining aggregate REP funds child backing once. Winning proofs
								authenticate their recorded depositors, while inherited losers retire without proofs.

fig-statoblast-system-decision-flow.ariaDescription:
Question, pool, escalation, fork, child migration, auction
								repair, fixed-outcome settlement, and unresolved recursive
								continuation flow.

fig-statoblast-auction-balance-sheet.ariaDescription:
A child pool before auction, after full auction repair, and after
								weak auction demand settles at the collateral actually raised.

fig-statoblast-oracle-flow.ariaDescription:
A solvency-sensitive operation either executes immediately with
								a valid cached price or stages behind a pending OpenOracle
								report.

fig-auction-lifecycle.ariaDescription:
Auction Lifecycle
					After migration closes, a child-pool shortfall can be repaired through auction. ETH bids restore collateral, while winning
					claims are settled into vault accounting. REP doesn't leave the system. Finalization accounts the ETH actually raised and
					rejects contribution-only ETH, so bidder settlement never depends on a donor.
fig-auction-lifecycle.ariaLabel: Migration closes, child pool shortfall is detected, auction starts, ETH bids are submitted, auction finalizes, and results settle into vault accounting.

fig-auction-clearing-ladder.ariaDescription: High-price bids are considered first. If cumulative demand reaches the ETH raise cap or REP sale cap, the first binding tick sets normal uniform clearing. If neither cap is reached, finalization selects bids at or above the cap-implied qualification tick and allocates the complete REP sale cap among them at one effective price. With no qualifying bids, every bid refunds.
fig-auction-clearing-ladder.ariaLabel: Auction demand is evaluated from high ticks to low ticks before uniform or underfunded clearing

children.text: first ETH or REP cap reached
complete REP cap shared pro rata

fig-zoltar-fork-branch-set.ariaDescription: Universe tree. A fork creates the full valid branch set; no branch is privileged by the contract.
fig-zoltar-fork-branch-set.ariaLabel: A parent universe forks into children for Invalid and each valid outcome.

fig-zoltar-threshold-deposit.ariaDescription: Threshold Deposit Split. The full parent-REP threshold leaves parent supply. Most is re-expressed as migratable child-REP credit; the haircut is not credited.
fig-zoltar-threshold-deposit.ariaLabel: Fork threshold deposit leaves the parent universe. After flooring the approximately 20 percent uncredited haircut, the remainder is an approximately 80 percent migration balance.

fig-zoltar-migration-reproduction.ariaDescription: Migration Balance Reproduction. Selecting multiple branches mints child REP in each selected child universe from the same migration balance.
fig-zoltar-migration-reproduction.ariaLabel: A migration balance can mint REP into one selected child or be reproduced across multiple selected children.

fig-zoltar-packed-scalar-answer.ariaDescription: Packed Scalar Answer. A scalar answer is easier to read as reserved bits, a namespace flag, and two payout fields: bits 254...240 must be zero, 0 in bit 255 is the invalid namespace, and 1 means the payout fields must sum to numTicks.
fig-zoltar-packed-scalar-answer.ariaLabel: A uint256 scalar answer uses the highest bit as a namespace flag, then packs first and second 120-bit payout numerators.

children.text: Bits 254...240 are reserved and must be zero.

fig-contract-interaction-map.ariaDescription: Three panels separate construction-time deployment, recurring market and oracle operations, and fork migration and backing repair. Repeated contracts preserve local reading order, short edge labels name each action, and the detailed table below gives the exact boundary.
fig-contract-interaction-map.ariaLabel: Zoltar and Statoblast contract interactions grouped into deployment, runtime, and fork phases

fig-liquidation-health-curve.ariaDescription: Required REP backing rises linearly with the REP per ETH price, while unlocked REP stays fixed. Crossing the available-REP line makes the selected vault liquidatable.
fig-liquidation-health-curve.ariaLabel: Vault backing requirement and liquidation threshold across REP per ETH prices

fig-statoblast-retention-utilization.ariaDescription: The annualized open-interest fee rises from about ten percent at zero utilization to about fifty percent at the eighty-percent utilization dip, then remains at that level as the per-second retention rate stays at its minimum.
fig-statoblast-retention-utilization.ariaLabel: Annualized open-interest fee across fee-eligible allowance utilization

fig-zoltar-fork-threshold-decay.ariaDescription: With the default threshold and burn divisors, each fork haircut leaves approximately ninety-nine percent of the previous generation's theoretical REP supply. The next fork threshold remains five percent of that declining supply.
fig-zoltar-fork-threshold-decay.ariaLabel: Theoretical REP supply and fork threshold across repeated forks

fig-open-oracle-arbitrager-lifecycle.ariaDescription: The arbitrager synchronizes approved OpenOracle reports, compares each report with executable Uniswap V3 liquidity, atomically hedges and disputes an eligible report, waits through later dispute rounds, atomically settles and withdraws exact balances, and only realizes profit when every configured read RPC serves the same twelfth-descendant block hash. Missing or contradictory evidence moves the durable position to recovery rather than releasing risk.
fig-open-oracle-arbitrager-lifecycle.ariaLabel: OpenOracle arbitrager execution and recovery lifecycle

children.text: retain risk · reconcile canonical evidence · retry or require operator

fig-open-oracle-arbitrager-profit.ariaDescription: Executable hedge proceeds or avoided WETH spending produce gross hedge profit. Entry gas, the signed worst-case slippage reserve, and the lifecycle gas reserve are subtracted before the strategy thresholds are tested. After execution, quote-time reserves are replaced by actual hedge and canonical gas evidence; realized profit is withheld until the exact lifecycle withdrawal reaches finality.
fig-open-oracle-arbitrager-profit.ariaLabel: OpenOracle arbitrager modeled and realized profit accounting

children.text: Modeled: conservative reserves · Tracked: actual hedge and entry gas · Realized: finalized exact withdrawal and actual lifecycle gas
